known_miss: The fourth query is a real miss at assist.similarity_floor. Its right answer scores 0.326 on this eight-item day, below the 0.35 floor measured against the 580-item archive. That is the floor doing its job on a corpus too small to hold a close match, not a retrieval defect, and it is why the bar tolerates one miss.
note: A WIRING CHECK, not an instrument. It proves the encoder loads, the committed vectors decode, a query returns a ranked list and a nonsense query returns the empty state. Five queries cannot measure retrieval quality - at n=5 the standard error at recall 0.8 is 0.18 - so the bar here is deliberately loose and stays loose. The quality measurement is tests/fixtures/search/retrieval-queries.json, run by backend/tests/test_retrieval_eval.py over the real archive. Each query names the CANARY it must retrieve rather than an item id or a rank: an id shifts when a canary is added, a rank shifts when a sibling changes, a canary name is stable. The test resolves the name to an item through that fixture's own title.

pass_bar.why: Four of five. A missed result costs a reader a convenience, so the bar is deliberately loose; the tight bars belong on the canaries, where a failure costs trust. It is not raised when the quality instrument improves - a five-query bar that moves is noise pretending to be a signal.
